findings.title: Async forEach is not awaited, so deletions and errors are not handled
findings.body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is async. Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the returned promises, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from await getCalendar, calendar?.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. The reschedule flow can return and send emails before the calendar/video events are actually deleted, and failed deletions become unhandled promise rejections. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires async deletion callbacks without awaiting them
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is given an async callback but the mutation never awaits the resulting promises. The request can complete before calendar/video events are deleted, and any rejection from await getCalendar, calendar?.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting is unhandled. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation uses unawaited async forEach for calendar deletions
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async ...) is not awaited. The outer handler later awaits apiDeletes, but these callbacks may not have finished or even pushed their work yet, and any rejection is unhandled. The callback also awaits calendar?.deleteEvent and pushes the resolved value, so apiDeletes would not contain a promise for that deletion anyway. Use Promise.all over deletion promises or a for...of loop and await the results.

findings.title: await apiDeletes does not await the promises in the array
findings.body: In the paid-cancellation path, await apiDeletes awaits the array object rather than its contents. Any integration deletion promises stored in apiDeletes are not awaited before the handler returns, so the response can finish while calendar/video deletions are still pending and rejections may be missed. Use await Promise.all(apiDeletes).

findings.title: Dynamic-import failure can bypass the Cal Video fallback in createMeeting
findings.body: getVideoAdapters now performs dynamic imports and can reject if an app chunk fails to load. The await on getVideoAdapters is outside the try/catch that implements the fallback to Cal Video, so an import failure causes createMeeting to reject instead of falling back. Move this call inside the try block or catch the error and use the fallback path.

findings.title: All app dynamic imports are started eagerly when appStore is imported
findings.body: The appStore object literal evaluates import() for every app as soon as this module is imported. This starts loading all app modules even when only one app is needed, which defeats lazy code-splitting and may increase startup latency. If an unused app's import rejects, it may also become an unhandled rejection. If lazy loading is intended, expose functions or getters that call import() on demand.

findings.title: getCalendar can reject on dynamic-import failure instead of returning null
findings.body: await appStore[...] can reject if the dynamic import fails, but getCalendar only handles missing or invalid apps by returning null. Several callers, such as CalendarManager.createEvent, await getCalendar without try/catch, so a failed app import can throw and break booking creation instead of being treated as an unavailable calendar. Consider catching import failures in getCalendar and returning null with a warning.
